A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same per-example-gradient study. Their main text, figures, equations, code examples, and Appendices A–F are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer-training comparisons, gradient-moment measurements, memory profiling, and MLP execution-time experiments, including batch-size and clipping analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original optimization experiments and reports additional Adam versus MicroAdam efficiency measurements across seven AlgoPerf workloads.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the second-moment EMA bias-correction denominator from 1−β1^t to 1−β2^t. The graph-surgery approach, vmap implementation strategy, and optimizer families remain the same. This establishes a pseudocode correction, not that the experimental implementations changed; the per-token second-moment quantity already appeared in v1 Appendix B.5.

E1.justification: v2 adds seven AlgoPerf efficiency workloads spanning WMT, FineWeb, ImageNet, fastMRI, and LibriSpeech, with transformer, ResNet, U-Net, Conformer, and DeepSpeech architectures. This substantially broadens evaluated data and task coverage beyond the retained C4 language-model experiments and MLP timing tests. The added outcomes concern computational efficiency.

E2.justification: The corresponding optimizer comparisons retain SignEMA, SignSGD, MicroSignSGD, Adam, MicroAdam, MicroAdamMSQ, and MicroAdamVar. The MLP comparison still evaluates graph surgery against vmap. The added AlgoPerf benchmarks extend the existing Adam–MicroAdam comparison without introducing another comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1 adds an efficiency-evaluation setup using AlgoPerf competition configurations, specified workload batch sizes, and removal of batch normalization. Figure 7 also changes gradient-moment aggregation from individual layers to averages across all layers. The retained C4 training budgets, learning-rate searches, and batch-size scaling protocols remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: The preconditioner diagnostic changes from a selected layer's moments and multiple layer-wise ratios in v1 Figure 6 to all-layer averages in v2 Figure 7. This revises the evidence presented about gradient-moment composition and removes that display's layer-level detail. Existing clipping, learning-rate, batch-size, and MLP size sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: No experimental replication counts, seed protocols, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added. Both versions retain the same EMA-based gradient-moment estimators; the revised diagnostic aggregation does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 2 adds substantial time and memory results across seven workloads, showing modest transformer overheads but much larger time costs for several other architectures. Appendix B.3 timing curves are updated, and Figure 7 reports aggregated moment curves. The retained Adam/MicroAdam/MicroAdamMSQ losses remain 3.06/3.16/3.05; v1's approximately 17% single-model overhead statement is omitted.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces the avg/EMA commutativity justification with an ordering constraint ensuring independence from within-batch indexing. The memory fact is condensed into Fact 2.1, removing v1 Appendix B.4's contradictory L<D example while retaining the input-versus-parameter-size argument. The main SNR, gradient-moment, and learning-rate-scaling derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary explicitly extend the computational contribution to per-token operations and foreground sequence architectures as a practical testbed. The central claims about tractable per-example statistics, applying sign late, and favoring mean-squared over variance-dominated Adam preconditioners remain.

C2.justification: v2 expands the architecture-dependent interpretation of computational feasibility and states the batch-normalization incompatibility of its vmap approach. It also presents the previously discussed per-activation quantity as a potentially useful per-token proxy and suggests extensions to higher-order statistics. The central optimizer interpretations and unresolved causal explanation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds the AlgoPerf API implementation, 2×4 TPU v5e setup, normalization modification, and global/per-device batch sizes in Table 1. Transformer hardware is specified more precisely. Algorithm 1 is expanded and partially corrected, while the extensive existing JAX examples and transformer hyperparameters are largely retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds context on gradient-noise statistics, Cockpit, ghost clipping, Functorch, and AlgoPerf, including references to McCandlish, Faghri, Gray, Goodfellow, Schneider, Dahl, and Kasimbeg. DrJAX and Griewank/Walther references disappear. The principal positioning relative to Dangel's second-moment computations and Wang/Aitchison's optimizer remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Section 2 are substantially rewritten. Memory/vmap opportunities now precede graph surgery, MicroAdam becomes an early running example, and appendix material is integrated into the main exposition. Section 3.2 and Appendix E are reorganized, with impact and author-contribution statements added.

P2.justification: The main text switches to two columns, with extensive figure relocation and redesign, revised axes and legends, a new efficiency chart and batch-size table, and expanded pseudocode formatting. Figure 6 swaps the lower MicroAdamVar/MicroAdamMSQ panels, but its caption and associated textual references retain their previous positions.

improvement.justification: The new efficiency measurements in Figure 2 give stronger evidence for where per-example computations are practical, and Appendix E.1 makes the relevant settings and normalization restriction explicit. Reorganized explanations and the bias-correction fix also help. These gains are tempered by the new Figure 6 panel-reference mismatch and reduced layer-level diagnostic detail. Overall, v2 provides a useful but bounded improvement around largely unchanged optimizer findings.
